Welcome toFletching CE Primary School
Welcome to our Fletching CE Primary School family where our Christian Ethos is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that we have a duty to provide all our children with opportunities to meet their spiritual and academic potential. Our tailored curriculum, driven by our values, is designed to develop our children's love of learning, encourage them to flourish into independent learners and prepare them for the next steps of their life journey.
At Fletching, we follow a therapeutic and nurturing approach which provides our children with a safe environment for them to thrive and 'grow in the love of God'. Our dedicated team of friendly staff work hard to make sure each child flourishes, both academically and socially. Our most recent OFSTED inspection (July 2022) it was noted that, 'Staff create a warm and welcoming atmosphere and the pupils feel part of the school family'. Furthermore, 'The Leaders use the school's values to drive the curriculum.'
We thank you for showing an interest in our school and hope that the information provided on our website will give you an insight into our school life.
Visits are warmly welcomed - we invite you to come and see our school in action and ask any questions you may have. Please contact Miss Tew in the School Office on 01825 722356 to make an appointment.

pageCache.pageTitle: Fletching Church of England Primary School - Phonics and Reading
pageCache.text:
Phonics and Reading
At Fletching Primary School, we believe that reading is an essential life skill and we prioritise teaching all children the skills and knowledge required to become fluent and confident readers and writers. We teach phonics and reading using the Little Wandle Revised Letters and Sounds Phonics Scheme across the whole school.
This programme has a robust framework for teaching, learning, and assessing development throughout five phases of learning. It focuses on positive experiences that build on children’s confidence and self-esteem as they see themselves progress rapidly towards becoming fluent readers, whilst avoiding unnecessary cognitive overload.
In Reception and Year 1, twenty minute daily phonics lessons are taught. The Little Wandle Scheme is a fast, fun and interactive approach where the children revisit and embed prior learning as well as learn new sounds and words. Regular assessment helps identify exactly where children are in their learning and teach to the child’s specific stage of development, as well as quickly identifying gaps in learning so that ‘keep up’ support can be applied.
Three times a week, the children read to an adult in a focused reading group using the Little Wandle Reading programme. The reading practice books that the children read at school and bring home are closely matched to the child’s phonological awareness, and they should be able to read it with 90% accuracy. This is to ensure they can enjoy and understand the story rather than just decode it. The same book will be focused throughout the whole week to revisit words, read with expression and intonation using the punctuation correctly and then finally comprehension of the story events as they discuss and elaborate on these.
We really appreciate your support and understanding of the theory behind only one book a week as it is very much about giving children ‘quality not quantity’ and embedding their learning securely into the long term memory.
From Year 2 children will progress to the Little Wandle fluency programme. This next stage focuses on developing all aspects of reading using a wide range of vibrant, diverse and engaging chapter books created by contemporary authors and illustrators. Any children who are identified as having larger gaps in their reading at Key stage 2 will be supported to fill the gaps in learning following the Rapid Catch Up programme. This is taught daily in small groups and regular assessments take place every four weeks.
Support for Phonics
Supporting your child with reading
Although your child will be taught to read at school, you can have a huge impact on their reading journey by continuing their practice at home.
There are two types of reading book that your child may bring home:
A reading practice book. This will be at the correct phonic stage for your child. They should be able to read this fluently and independently.
A sharing book. Your child will not be able to read this on their own. This book is for you both to read and enjoy together.
Reading practice book
This book has been carefully matched to your child’s current reading level. If your child is reading it with little help, please don’t worry that it’s too easy – your child needs to develop fluency and confidence in reading.
Listen to them read the book. Remember to give them lots of praise – celebrate their success! If they can’t read a word, read it to them. After they have finished, talk about the book together.
In order to encourage your child to become a lifelong reader, it is important that they learn to read for pleasure. The sharing book is a book they have chosen for you to enjoy together.
Please remember that you shouldn’t expect your child to read this alone. Read it to or with them. Discuss the pictures, enjoy the story, predict what might happen next, use different voices for the characters, explore the facts in a non-fiction book. The main thing is that you have fun!
We have a wonderful library at the school stocked with a wide range of books of many genres. Each class has a weekly library visit in which they can select a reading for pleasure book to read and bring home to share.

pageCache.text:
Admissions
East Sussex County Council makes the arrangements for the admission of children to Fletching CE Primary School who will be joining Reception each September.
Parents who are seeking admission to the school for their children at age 4 should refer to the East Sussex County Council website for a detailed description of the process:
Apply for a school place | East Sussex County Council
The admissions booklets can be viewed or downloaded and are updated annually.The Published Admissions Number (PAN) for Fletching CE Primary School is 15 places.
Copies of these publications and further information can be obtained from:
The Schools Admission Team, Education Department, County Hall, St Anne’s Crescent, Lewes. BN7 1SG
If you have a child in years 1 to 6 and are considering moving them to Fletching School, please contact the school office to ascertain whether there is a space and/or arrange to have a tour of the school. pageCache.text:
Home School Values
Home School Values is a resource to help strengthen links with our parents by sharing with them the Value in Focus each half term. The values sheets are full of fun activities for the family to do together alongside topics to stimulate discussion and reflection.
Home School Values is designed to promote spiritual and moral development. It is not homework and is used most effectively when parents are really enthusiastic about exploring the value at home with their children. Parents will need to use discretion when deciding which parts of each issue of Home School Values are most appropriate to the age of their children.
Please click on the links below to view the 'Home School Value' sheet.

Wonderful Inquisitive Nurture
